title: Sub-teams & Initiatives
text:
How Sub-teams Work
Each sub-team is a volunteer working group centered on a specific methodological or operational topic. Participation is entirely flexible, members may observe, contribute, take a leadership role, or propose a new sub-team at any time. The Leadership Team provides mentorship and consultation to anyone starting or stepping into a leadership role.
The IDSWG actively welcomes members from patient advocacy organizations. Patient advocates participate as full members across sub-teams, particularly in NEED, Patient Engagement, and the KOL Lecture Series, and bring perspectives that improve the relevance and accessibility of the group’s scientific outputs.
To join a sub-team or propose a new one, contact Bob, Mercedeh, or Alex, contact details are on the About page.

title: Sub-teams & Initiatives
text:
Patient Engagement Sub-team
The Patient Engagement sub-team, previously led by Deborah Collyar of Patient Advocates in Research (PAIR), is currently seeking a new leader.
Patient engagement is not a peripheral activity for the IDSWG, it is embedded in the group’s mission. Innovative trial designs should reduce patient burden, reflect what patients actually care about measuring, and be accessible to the populations who most need them. The Patient Engagement Sub-team works at the intersection of trial methodology and patient advocacy, ensuring that design innovation serves patients rather than simply optimizing operational or statistical metrics.
Activities have included joint workshops with patient communities, consultation on endpoint selection for rare disease trials, and contributions to the NEED Sub-team’s work on evidence standards for rare diseases.
If you are interested in leading this sub-team, please contact Mercedeh Ghadessi (mercedeh.ghadessi@bayer.com).

title: Randomization Working Group
text:
Overview
The IDSWG Randomization Working Group is a joint initiative with PSI/EFSPI and ASA-BIOP, co-chaired by Johannes Krisam, Ph.D. and Kerstine Carter (both Boehringer Ingelheim) and Alex Sverdlov, Ph.D. (Novartis).
The WG focuses on bringing awareness to modern randomization approaches that go beyond standard permuted-block methods, improving efficiency, balancing prognostic factors, and supporting the use of covariate-adaptive and response-adaptive designs.
Named PSI Special Interest Group of the Year in June 2025.

title: NEED, Rare Diseases Sub-team
text:
Overview
The NEED Sub-team is co-led by Sammi Tang (Astellas) and Mercedeh Ghadessi (Bayer). It focuses on the nature and extent of evidence needed to support drug approval in rare disease settings, where small patient populations, natural history variability, and limited precedent create unique methodological challenges.
Patient perspectives are central to the sub-team’s work. Rare disease trials often involve patient populations with few treatment options, strong advocacy communities, and high stakes in regulatory decisions. The sub-team works to ensure that evidence standards reflect what matters to patients and their families, not only what is statistically tractable.

title: MPWG: Basket Trials Sub-stream
text:
Overview
The Basket Trials sub-stream focuses on the design, simulation, and real-world application of confirmatory basket trials, studies that evaluate a single treatment across multiple diseases or molecular subtypes simultaneously.
Lead: Robert A. Beckman, M.D. (Georgetown University)
Members: Martin Posch (Med U Vienna), Olivier Collignon (GSK), Thomas Gwise (ex-FDA), Nicole Li (BeiGene), Kit Roes (EMA), Kristine Broglio (AstraZeneca), Cindy Lu (AstraZeneca), Philip He (Daiichi Sankyo), Heng Zhou (Merck), Helen Zhou (GSK), Cong Chen (Merck), Linchen He (Novartis), Valeriy Korostyshevskiy (Georgetown), Sathvik Narayana (Albany Medical College), Sammi Tang (Astellas), Ruixiao Lu (Alumis), Patrick Roney (Georgetown)

title: MPWG: Basket Trials Sub-stream
text:
Focus Areas

Educating the scientific community on basket trial methodology, benefits, and appropriate use
Developing confirmatory basket trial designs with rigorous Type I error control
Simulation-based evaluation of operating characteristics across disease settings
Real-world data applications: using external data to inform basket trial design and analysis

title: StatBridge Future Leaders Program
text:
About the Program
The StatBridge Future Leaders Program is an IDSWG initiative designed to support early-career biostatisticians and data scientists at the intersection of academic training and clinical practice. The program grew from a recognized gap: biostatisticians emerging from graduate programs often have strong methodological foundations but limited exposure to the practical realities of pharmaceutical drug development, regulatory interactions, and cross-functional team dynamics.
StatBridge addresses that gap through mentorship, structured exposure to IDSWG sub-team work, and professional development opportunities within a global community of quantitative scientists.
Program Co-Leads:

Bryan McComb, Ph.D., Associate Director of Biostatistics, Pfizer; Co-Leader of External Collaborations, IDSWG
Courtney Henry, Ph.D., GSK; Co-Leader of Community, IDSWG

title: StatBridge Future Leaders Program
text:
What We Offer

  
    
    Mentorship
    Pairing with experienced biostatisticians from pharma, academia, and regulatory settings. Mentors offer career guidance, project feedback, and professional network introductions.
  
  
    
    Sub-team Exposure
    Opportunities to observe and contribute to active IDSWG sub-teams, gaining experience in collaborative scientific work, publication processes, and regulatory engagement.
  
  
    
    Presentation Opportunities
    Pathways to present at IDSWG events, including the annual meeting, KOL Lecture Series, and major conferences such as JSM and SCT.
  
  
    
    Community
    Access to a global network of quantitative scientists from pharmaceutical companies, academic institutions, biotech firms, and health authorities across the US, Europe, and Japan.

title: StatBridge Future Leaders Program
text:
Who Should Join
The StatBridge program is designed for:

Graduate students in biostatistics, statistics, data science, or related quantitative fields who are interested in pharmaceutical or clinical research careers
Early-career biostatisticians (typically within the first five years post-PhD or MS) working in academia, industry, or government who want to deepen their exposure to innovative trial design
Academic researchers who collaborate with industry or regulatory bodies and want to strengthen those connections

There are no formal requirements for participation. The program is open to members from all geographic locations and institutional backgrounds. Students and early-career professionals with backgrounds in patient advocacy, health communications, or clinical research operations are also welcome, the program values diverse perspectives on what makes trial design work in practice.

title: StatBridge Future Leaders Program
text:
Get Involved
As a participant or mentee: Reach out to Bryan McComb or Courtney Henry to express your interest. A brief introduction and statement of what you hope to gain from the program is sufficient to get started.
As a mentor: Experienced IDSWG members with 10+ years in the field are encouraged to volunteer as mentors. The commitment is flexible, typically one to two hours per month.
As an organizational partner: If your institution, company, or program is interested in collaborating, for example, by co-hosting a workshop, please contact the co-leads.

  Ready to Connect?
  Contact either StatBridge co-lead to learn more or express your interest in the program.

title: New Publication: Cell and Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases

The NEED Sub-team’s latest paper has been published in Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science:

title: DahShu Innovative Design Scientific Working Group
text:
Who We Are
The DahShu Innovative Design Scientific Working Group (IDSWG) is a cross-industry scientific community with approximately 200 members drawn from pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology firms, academic medical centers, contract research organizations, health authorities, and patient advocacy organizations across the United States, Europe, and Japan.
Members share a common premise: well-designed clinical trials are among the most powerful tools available for bringing safe and effective treatments to patients. Statisticians, clinicians, pharmacometricians, regulators, patient advocates, and operations professionals work across sub-teams to advance that premise through published methodology, regulatory engagement, and practical guidance.

title: About the IDSWG
text:
Membership
Current membership stands at approximately 200 members representing pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology firms, contract research organizations, academic medical centers, health authorities, and patient advocacy organizations across the United States, Europe, and Japan.
Patient advocates are full and valued members of the IDSWG, not external consultants. The group’s Patient Engagement Sub-team (currently seeking a new leader) focuses specifically on ensuring that trial designs reflect patient priorities, burden, and experience. Embedding patient perspectives from the earliest design stages is a core principle of the group’s work.
Membership is open and free of charge. To join or update contact information, reach out to the leadership team directly or connect via the get involved form.

title: Go-Live Checklist — DahShu IDSWG Website
text:
Common Questions
Q: Do I need to know coding to maintain the site?
A: No. Most updates (news posts, publications, KOL schedule) involve editing plain text. The README has a step-by-step cheat sheet.
Q: What if something breaks after I push a change?
A: The GitHub Actions log (under Actions tab in your repo) will show what went wrong. The previous working version is always in the git history — you can revert by undoing your last commit.
Q: How do I add a co-maintainer?
A: Add them as a Collaborator on the GitHub repository (Settings → Collaborators). They’ll be able to push changes that trigger auto-deployment.

title: MPWG Publication: Company Sponsored Platform Trials
text:
Skip to main content



  










The Master Protocol Working Group has published a new paper in Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science:
Company Sponsored Platform Trials: Recommendations and Lessons Learned from Cross-Industry Interviews Wu, Y., Lu, C., Aregay, M. et al.
This paper reports findings from cross-industry interviews examining the design, operational, and strategic challenges of company-sponsored platform trials. It offers practical recommendations for organizations considering this trial structure.
The MPWG is a joint working group co-chaired by Cindy Lu (AstraZeneca) and Robert Beckman (Georgetown University), operating under the ASA, DahShu IDSWG, and BSWG umbrella.
Read the paper, doi:10.1007/s43441-025-00792-0

title: Randomization Working Group Named PSI SIG of the Year
text:
Skip to main content



  










The IDSWG Randomization Working Group has been named PSI Special Interest Group of the Year for 2025, a recognition of its sustained contributions to randomization methodology in clinical trials.
The Randomization WG is co-chaired by Johannes Krisam and Kerstine Carter (both Boehringer Ingelheim) and Alex Sverdlov (Novartis). The group currently has approximately 50 active and inactive members spanning pharmaceutical industry (19), academia (24), and other organizations (7), with representation across Europe/UK and the USA.
The WG’s work focuses on moving beyond standard permuted-block randomization to bring awareness of modern methodological advances in the field. Activities include monthly member meetings, open learning sessions, a dedicated website, and a growing library of publications, slide sets, and educational resources.
Congratulations to the Randomization WG team on this well-deserved recognition.

title: Annual Meeting Recap, September 24, 2025
text:
Skip to main content



  










The IDSWG held its annual face-to-face meeting on September 24, 2025, bringing together members from across the group’s sub-teams and initiatives.
The evening opened with welcome remarks from Chair Bob Beckman, followed by introductory presentations on the IDSWG, DahShu, and collaboration opportunities with the Bayesian Scientific Working Group (BSWG). Bryan McComb presented the StatBridge Future Leaders Program, highlighting the initiative’s goals and upcoming activities.
Sub-team reports covered the Master Protocol Working Group (Concept, Methodology and Framework; Regulatory), the Randomization Working Group, the AI/ML Sub-team, the NEED Sub-team for Rare Diseases, and the KOL Lecture Series.
Key updates from the meeting:

The Concept, Methodology and Framework sub-stream of the MPWG is undergoing a reboot under new leadership from Bryan McComb and Courtney Henry. New members are welcome.
The Regulatory Sub-team is seeking volunteers to support the 2020–2025 Systematic Literature Review update.
Two leadership positions remain open for the 2025–2026 term, nominations are welcome.

The next annual meeting date will be announced via the DahShu community. Subscribe to receive updates.

title: Resources
text:
FDA Guidance

  
    FDA, November 2019
    Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials of Drugs and Biologics
    Core FDA guidance on pre-specified adaptations, alpha control, and operational integrity in adaptive trials.
    Download PDF
  
  
    FDA, September 2022
    Master Protocols: Efficient Clinical Trial Design Strategies
    FDA guidance on basket, umbrella, and platform trial design, covering estimands, statistical analysis plans, and regulatory interaction.
    Download PDF
  
  
    FDA, December 2023
    Decentralized Clinical Trials for Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices
    Final guidance on remote assessments, local healthcare providers, and digital data collection in decentralized trials.
    FDA guidance portal
  
  
    FDA, January 2025
    Considerations for the Design and Conduct of Externally Controlled Trials
    Guidance on using real-world data as a control arm, with particular relevance for rare diseases and pediatric populations.
    FDA guidance portal
  
  
    FDA, January 2026 New
    Use of Bayesian Methodology in Clinical Trials of Drug and Biological Products (Draft)
    Landmark draft guidance covering Bayesian approaches to primary inference in pivotal trials, adaptive designs, rare disease trials, and incorporation of external data including real-world evidence. Covers pre-specification requirements, prior selection, success criteria, and simulation. Open for public comment; comments due March 13, 2026. Docket: FDA-2025-D-3217.
    Federal Register notice
  

  
    FDA, February 2026 New
    Plausible Mechanism Framework for Individualized Therapies Targeting Specific Genetic Conditions (Draft)
    Draft guidance establishing a framework for approval of highly individualized therapies (genome editing, RNA-based) for ultra-rare diseases where conventional randomized trials are not feasible. Describes conditions for meeting the substantial evidence of effectiveness standard via mechanistic evidence. Notes master protocols as a design option for evaluating multiple variants under a single application. Open for comment; comments due April 27, 2026. Docket: FDA-2026-D-1256.
    Federal Register notice

The Methodology and Concept sub-stream focuses on the theoretical and applied foundations of master protocol design, including framework development, estimand considerations, simulation methodology, and the conceptual distinctions between basket, umbrella, and platform trial structures.

title: MPWG: Patient Engagement Sub-stream
text:
Overview
The Patient Engagement sub-stream focuses on incorporating patient and caregiver perspectives into master protocol trial design, including endpoint selection, trial accessibility, participation burden, and communication of complex study structures to patients and advocates.
Status: This sub-stream is on hold pending new leadership. It is expected to reconvene in early 2026.
Previous contributors include: Deborah Collyar (Patient Advocates in Research, PAIR)

title: MPWG: Patient Engagement Sub-stream
section: Why Patient Engagement Matters in Master Protocols
text:
Why Patient Engagement Matters in Master Protocols
Master protocol trials, particularly platform and basket designs, are operationally complex and can span years or decades. Ensuring that patients understand what they are enrolling in, that endpoints reflect outcomes meaningful to them, and that participation burden is minimized requires active patient engagement from the design stage onward.
Prior MPWG work has addressed patient engagement directly:

Huml RA, Collyar D, Antonijevic Z, Beckman RA et al. Aiding the adoption of master protocols by optimizing patient engagement. Therapeutic Innovation and Regulatory Science, 57: 1136–1147 (2023).

title: Master Protocols (ASA-DahShu MPWG)
text:
Overview
The ASA-DahShu IDSWG Master Protocol Working Group (MPWG) is a joint effort co-chaired by Cindy Lu (AstraZeneca) and Robert Beckman, M.D. (Georgetown University), operating under the American Statistical Association, DahShu IDSWG, and Bayesian Scientific Working Group umbrella.
The MPWG focuses on the methodology, regulatory landscape, and operational implementation of master protocols, covering basket, umbrella, and platform trials that evaluate multiple treatments or patient populations within a single overarching study framework.

title: Real-World Evidence (RWE) Sub-team
text:
Overview
The RWE Sub-team is chaired by James Chuo (Gilead). It focuses on the appropriate use of real-world data and real-world evidence, from electronic health records, claims databases, patient registries, and other sources, in clinical development, including external control arms and pragmatic trial designs.
Current members: James Chuo (Gilead), Shikai Jin (Gilead), Andy Surianch (Genesis Research), Wen-Hsing Wu (Moderna), Victoria Strauss (Boehringer Ingelheim).
The sub-team’s 2025 highlights include a poster at ISPE 2025 on aligning data types with research needs. Planned work for 2025–2026 includes identifying key areas and unmet needs for RWE in the pharmaceutical industry, targeting at least one white paper or conference presentation, and applying emerging technologies for better RWE use and interpretation.
The sub-team pays particular attention to methodological standards and regulatory expectations governing RWE, including the FDA’s framework for real-world evidence and the EMA’s reflection paper on real-world data.
